utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. A special welcome today to the parties and the accused in my new capacity as presiding and pre-appeal judge of this case. May I ask Mr. Registrar, please, to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution today, myself, Norman Farrell, and with me is Ms. Helen Brady, Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind and our case manager, Ms. Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Mitko Naumovski, attorney at law from Zagreb, representing Dario Kordic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Bozidar Kovacic. I am representing Mario Cerkez, together with my colleague Goran Mikulicic in his capacity as co-counsel in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I take the opportunity to start the other way around than usual, and I ask the accused themselves whether they have any complaints about the Detention Unit. Do you have any special health problems or anything you want to address directly to the Chamber, or to me? May we start with Mr. Kordic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE APPELLANT KORDIC: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank God, I feel well. I do not have any objections as to the conditions in the Detention Unit, and thank you for your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated, please. And Mr. Cerkez, please. THE APPELLANT CERKEZ: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for asking. I'm fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated, then. I'm aware that both parties, but first of all the Defence, and primarily the accused themselves, are waiting for a decision on a motion to set dates for oral hearing of the case. Please accept that not only me, but the entire Trial Chamber, regrets that no final date for a hearing of this case can be set today. You know, the Appeals Chamber is seized with numerous cases, some even waiting longer than your case. In general, this is no apology and no excuse at all for the delay. The only thing I can promise you today is that we try to do our very best to hear the case as soon as possible. But admittedly, I myself and my colleagues, we feel uncomfortable with the situation where, since such a long period of time has elapsed since the trial judgement has been handed down, it's not possible to set even a date for the appeal. Let's hope that we can overcome as soon as possible the obstacles. Let us check together what are the open motions to be decided. May I first turn with Mr. Kordic's notice of OTP's non-compliance with its Rule 68 obligations, filed in March this year. May I hear the parties first on this issue. Let's start with the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we have explained our submissions in our motion, and I believe that the Prosecutor has already responded and addressed all of the issues. So we are now waiting for your decisions, and the instruction as to how to proceed. Should our motion be granted, then we would certainly need a certain amount of time to prepare our motion, the one that we requested leave to submit. I overestimated the time necessary for that, and I said that should the motion be accepted, that we would perhaps need two weeks to file an additional motion. However, in the meantime, I have given it a bit more thought and realised that we would need a minimum of three to four weeks to submit a new motion. This is just my best estimate. I cannot tell you exactly how much time we would require to submit the additional motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In case leave would be granted as from the day of granting leave. Any additional remarks by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it's for the Bench to decide as soon as possible on this issue, and you will receive as soon as possible a decision on the primary question, whether or not to grant leave. Then we have two motions from Mr. Kordic, one motion from Mr. Cerkez, under Rule 115. Let us once again start with the two ones of Mr. Kordic. Here a decision will be rendered soon. However, a decision by the Bench. Please understand that, for the time being, I can't give you any further explanations. What about Mr. Cerkez's motion on 115?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the submissions, including the response and the reply, have been completed. All of the arguments have been presented, and it is up to the Court to decide as to how to proceed pursuant to the motion for additional evidence based on Rule 115, that is, in what stages they will decide what criteria they will apply in view of the case law of this Tribunal, and at what time the Judges will decide to convene an oral hearing to hear oral submissions. I don't know whether that's going to be prior to the issuance of a Rule 115 decision, or once they have decided on the admissibility of the motion. I believe that the case law has been changing in this regard, but we do not have any additional proposals or suggestions, aside from what we have already argued. We are now waiting for the Chamber to decide on this issue before a Pre-Appeal conference, because the decision is likely to have some consequences on how the appeal will go. But before you ask the question, and I think that you will probably ask me, let me just say that whatever we have so far received from the OTP, including material pursuant to Rule 68, we do not intend to use this for any additional motions pursuant to Rule 115. With one caveat in respect of the so-called fourth submission for additional evidence in the Blaskic case. I should certainly like to see this first, and then make a decision, though I don't see any significant changes taking place in that regard. With your permission, Your Honour, before we used to be asked whether we wished to speak our mother tongue or English, and let me just ask the question now: I would like to speak my mother tongue. If you should decide contrary to this, then I will address the Court in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have no problems with this. You only should be aware that sometimes the one or other slight problem might be -- may arise from translation. But being capable of both languages, you will immediately identify yourself when there seems to be a mistake or a misunderstanding. Please advise the Judge or the Bench when this should happen. Otherwise we are prepared, of course, to listen to you in the language you commonly use. Thank you for this specific request. So I noticed your caveat. I understand your caveat, and so on the other hand, you will understand that time is not yet ripe for a final decision, and we have to look forward to this fourth motion in the Blaskic case you just mentioned before. Thank you for these additional remarks. Just to clarify as regards the two motions by Mr. Kordic: They were those for access to ex parte submissions in Mr. Cerkez's Rule 115 motion, and there a decision will follow as soon as possible, hopefully in the course of this week already. In preparation of the case, I have one additional problem. The Prosecutor has filed the 26th of September, 2003 a motion, confidential and ex parte. Therefore, I can't, it's self-understanding, not go into any details. May I ask the Prosecution whether it's -- what are the reasons. Is it necessary having to go into detail? That is, this motion is filed ex parte. Because I think it could infringe one party's right to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the simple answer is that the original protective measure order of July 31st indicated that the decision and the contents of the decision for protective measures, which, as you know, the motion of September 26th is an attempt to vary that, that original decision of July 31st indicated that -- imposed certain protective requirements on it which would, at least in our interpretation, preclude us from filing it in any other form than ex parte.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As I said already beforehand, I think no decision by the entire Bench is necessary. Do you see from your side any obstacle to file this motion once again confidentially only?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: If I could respond to that by having a chance to review the decision to see if there's anything in there that would require some form of possible redaction to ensure compliance with the previous decisions relating to the content of that, I can either get back to your Senior Legal Officer or I can file something, if possible, in redacted form, if that may assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You should only know that I would prefer, if possible, and inasmuch as possible, to file this confidentially only, because I really believe that the other party has a right as well to be heard of this and to respond, if necessary. But I think the procedure suggested by you is the appropriate one.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the parties: For the time being, are there any other issues to be discussed in the framework of the Status Conference? The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Kordic has no special issues to raise at today's Status Conference, but we would simply like to inform you that today I was not able to gain access to the Hadzihasanovic material in accordance with the previous decisions of this Chamber. The reasons were technical and I assume that the materials will be mailed to me shortly, so that within 10 or 15 days we will be able to inform the Chamber as to whether we shall use some of these materials or not. I had intended to take all this with me now I'm in The Hague today but I was not able to. In any case, the Defence of Mr. Kordic is encouraged by what Your Honour has said today as to speeding up and expediting these proceedings, and we are awaiting your decisions in this respect. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me just clarify. The decision has been filed on the materials in the Hadzihasanovic case, and we took it as granted that you would have access already today. When do you intend to leave The Hague, may I ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the decision, Your Honour. I'm leaving tomorrow, but the Registry says that, due to lack of time, they are unable to prepare this material. They have to make sure that there isn't something ex parte in the material, to avoid any confusion. And as far as I was able to understand, the lady in charge of this is on sick leave. However, I feel that there will not be a problem. If I can't get the material today, I assume it will be mailed to me within a few days. What is important is that we have established contact, and I trust that this will all be resolved soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can we conclude by saying that in case you don't have access to this material within the next seven days, you will alert the Trial Chamber that the necessary message be taken that you can have access to the material as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, Your Honour, we will apply to you for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other issues by the Defence of Mr. Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour, we have no further issues to raise. And we think we will not need to file any further motions, apart from what was discussed today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you for your inquiry, Your Honour. The Prosecution has nothing further to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have to thank you for this Status Conference. Let's once again be assured that we try to be as expeditious as possible. The Status Conference is hereby adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.56 p.m.
